title: Profile Calibration
concept: Together, you map which way each of you leans, plan first or mood first, where you tend to misread each other, and what each of you needs to stay steady. It’s a shared language, not a diagnosis.
whenToUse: Early on, or when the old fight comes round again (one of you “cold”, the other “too much”), and before you change how you handle conflict. Nobody has to complete this, and you can stop at any time.
steps: Each of you scores your own lean from 1 to 10, plan first to mood first. It’s a lean, not a life sentence.
Share one way you show love that gets misread.
Share one thing you need to stay calm in a fight.
Each write two lines for your plan for settling after a hard moment, and agree one signal for “I’m close to my limit”.
Pick one translation habit for 14 days. At the monthly part of your Weekly Reset, decide whether it stays.
In the Field App, each of you answers 44 questions on your own. The Layer Scan report then shows where you differ most, layer by layer.

phrases.text: I show love by solving. Tell me if you need warmth first.
I need the feeling named before we fix it.
I can pause; I’ll be ready at ___. I’m not leaving you.

working: B (mood first) is hurt, and A (plan first) jumps to fixes, then catches it: “Warmth first. I’m here. That sounded painful.” Once B feels heard, B asks for the fixes. Same fixes, different order.
notWorking: A: “I’m fixing it because I love you, so stop being emotional.” B: “If you loved me you’d feel this with me.” Each is telling the truth about how they love, and using it as an accusation.
activity: Do the Profile Calibration sheet together (30 to 40 minutes), or each answer the app questions separately. Put your two-line plans where you’ll both see them before a hard conversation.
warn: Do not ask your partner to show their answers. Never use a profile as a label to win an argument. Afraid of your partner, or not free to say no? Stop: use the Help Lines.
note: Layer Scan: the app’s quick check for when something feels off and you can’t say what. It shows where your answers are furthest apart across five layers, so you have somewhere specific to start. Your answers stay on your phone.
